The IRW table holds exactly two items, SS1 and SS4 (663 responses each, resp 1-5), taken by data/jeilani_2024_academic_stress.py as the raw .xlsx columns of that name (figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.26820745.v4, CC0). The F1000Research article (13:1108, PMC12141996) reproduces no item wording at all; its Table 2 and the deposit's 'Measurement and Model fit.jpg' both load the social-support factor on SO1-SO4 only, so the paper never names SS1 or SS4. The deposit's remaining files are two more .jpg figures and a t-statistic .docx (checked: AMOS output, no items). What IS recoverable is the subscale, not the item: the paper cites the MSPSS (ref 35, Calderon et al. 2021) and the support block's correlation matrix over the 663 rows splits cleanly into three quartets -- {SSF1,SSF3,SSF4,SSF2_001} r=0.54-0.68 (family, SSF1's .sav label is 'I get the emotional help and support I need from my family'), {SSF2,SS1,SSF2_002,SS4} r=0.56-0.69 (friends), and {SO1,SO2,SO3,SO4} r=0.69-0.74 (significant other, all four .sav labels are 'special person' items) -- with cross-block r only 0.28-0.47. So SS1 and SS4 are two of the four MSPSS friends items (canonical items 6, 7, 9, 12), and the two columns the .xlsx header misspells as 'SSF2'/'SSF2_002' are the other two. That pins the subscale but not which friends item each code is, and the deposit's within-subscale numbering is demonstrably NOT canonical MSPSS order: the .sav's SO1-SO4 labels are MSPSS items 10, 5, 1, 2 in that order. With no per-item statistics published for SS1/SS4 anywhere, all 12 assignments of two codes to four friends items remain equally consistent with every available fact, so no defensible item_text can be written and none was. No __items.csv written; no mapping_verification row written either, per Step 5b ('a blocked table has no live item text, so it cannot carry a verification outcome of any kind'), and hence no verify_jeilani_2024_social_support.R. Pass with a real caveat. (1) FALLBACK LANGUAGE SHAPE: the CESD-10 was administered to these Korean homecare workers in Korean, and no Korean wording exists in scope -- the deposit is an English-labelled .sav (S2 File, all 38 variable labels and every value label ASCII, zero Hangul), the only questionnaire supplement S1 Fig is the Copenhagen Burnout Inventory GIF, not the CESD-10, and the paper body prints no Korean. So English sits in the base fields, language=Korean, the four _translated columns are empty, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. (2) THE ENGLISH IS THE STUDY'S OWN SHORT DESCRIPTORS, NOT ITEM SENTENCES: the paper names the ten items as 'loss of interest, trouble concentrating, feeling depressed, feeling tired or low in energy, feeling afraid, trouble falling asleep, feeling alone, and finding it hard to get going' plus 'feel pretty good and generally satisfied', and the .sav variable labels carry the same ten phrases. Canonical Andresen CES-D-10 sentences were deliberately NOT substituted: this Korean version's item 1 is 'loss of interest', which is not canonical item 1 ('I was bothered by things that usually don't bother me'), so upgrading to canonical wording would have shipped a different instrument's sentences. Terse in, terse out. (3) ONE TRANSCRIPTION CHOICE NAMED: the .sav label for cesd10 reads 'finding it hard to get along'; the paper's own list reads 'finding it hard to get going', which is also the canonical CES-D item ('I could not get going'). The paper's wording ships and the .sav label is treated as a typo. cesd4's label is 'tired or low in energy' and the paper's 'feeling tired or low in energy' ships. En dashes in the paper's anchors ('1-2 days', '3-4 days', '5-7 days') were written as ASCII hyphens. (4) MAPPING IS data_labels AND NEEDS NO ROUTE: data/jeon_2019_cbi_cesd.py melts the source columns cesd1..cesd10 by name with no rename, so the IRW item code IS the .sav column name, and that column's own variable label names its content -- the exempt first derivation pattern. Corroborated independently anyway: the paper lists the eight negative-affect descriptors in exactly cesd1,2,3,4,6,7,9,10 order and says the two positive items are 'items 5 and 8', matching the labels at cesd5/cesd8. (5) RESP DIRECTION CHECKED AGAINST THE PUBLISHED TOTAL, not assumed: the paper states '0 = very rarely...; 3 = almost always or 5-7 days' and that items 5 and 8 are reverse-scored for the total. Recoding the .sav by its value-label strings exactly as the script does and reversing 5 and 8 gives total mean 7.80 / SD 3.82, identical to the paper's reported 7.80 (3.82); leaving them raw gives 6.06 / 4.39. The live table stores the raw direction (cesd5 mean 1.18 and cesd8 mean 0.95 vs 0.38-0.63 for the eight negative items, and cesd5-cesd8 r = +0.52 while both correlate only +0.05..+0.20 with the negative block), so the ascending-frequency anchors shipped here are the correct per-item direction and no reverse-scoring is baked into resp. (6) RIGHTS: no block. The CES-D (Radloff 1977, NIMH) and the CESD-10 short form carry no quotable fee or no-redistribution clause, and the shipped English comes from a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article. RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate, the table is written; only a newly published Korean CESD-10 form from these authors would change what ships.
